experiments.name: Calibration of long-stem standard platinum resistance thermometers at the ITS-90 triple point of argon (83.8058 K) in a liquid-nitrogen-cooled sealed argon cell (Isotech Model 471)
experiments.plain_name: Calibrate a precision platinum thermometer at the melting point of frozen argon
experiments.description: Secondary-laboratory realization of the argon triple point, the lowest ITS-90 fixed point used for long-stem SPRTs: a pressurised sealed cell of pure argon inside an 8 L stainless container is frozen with liquid nitrogen poured through the re-entrant well, then the SPRT is inserted and calibrated on the roughly 4 h melting plateau (k=2 uncertainty 0.5 mK in the Isotech apparatus; NIST lists 0.14 mK for its realization).

requirements.rationale: The calibration point is the ITS-90 triple point of argon, 83.8058 K; the cell space must be held there during the melt.
requirements.document_title: Argon Triple Point - Isotech Model 471: Further Refinement (J. Tavener, Isotech Seminar 2018)
requirements.location: Slide 5 'What is the Argon Triple Point?'
requirements.quote: 3.3.1.3. The Triple Point Of Argon (83.8058 K) to the Triple Point of Water (273.16K).

requirements.rationale: The argon sample must first be frozen, so the apparatus must reach below the argon triple point (-189.3442 C = 83.8058 K); the Isotech apparatus uses an LN2 bath near -195 C.
requirements.document_title: Standard Platinum Resistance Thermometer Calibration Laboratory (SPRTCL), NIST
requirements.quote: This range spans from the triple point of argon (-189.3442 °C) to the freezing point of silver (961.78 °C).

requirements.rationale: The Isotech procedure freezes the cell with liquid nitrogen through its re-entrant well; NIST has also developed a closed-cycle argon apparatus, so LN2 is not strictly mandatory.
requirements.document_title: Argon Triple Point - Isotech Model 471: Further Refinement (J. Tavener, Isotech Seminar 2018)
requirements.quote: It has re-entrant tube to accommodate either a funnel of liquid nitrogen for cooling or an SPRT for calibration

requirements.rationale: A premium calibration uses the melting plateau, which lasted about 4 hours (14400 s); the cold environment must be sustained that long.

experiments.name: Calibration of capsule-type SPRTs and rhodium-iron thermometers at the ITS-90 triple points of equilibrium hydrogen, neon, oxygen and argon (13.8033-83.8058 K) in sealed cells inside a vacuum-isolated closed-cycle cryostat by the calorimetric intermittent-heating method
experiments.plain_name: Calibrate small cryogenic thermometers at the melting points of frozen hydrogen, neon, oxygen and argon
experiments.description: National-metrology-institute realization of the cryogenic gas triple points following the BIPM CCT guide: sealed (multi-compartment) copper or stainless-steel cells are suspended inside temperature-controlled isothermal shields within a vacuum jacket, cooled (nowadays) by a two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler, and melted by intermittent heat pulses while capsule SPRTs read the plateau.

requirements.rationale: The four triple points span 13.8033 K (e-H2) to 83.8058 K (Ar); the cryostat must hold the cell at each of them.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Cryogenic Fixed Points (B Fellmuth, E Mendez-Lango, T Nakano, F Sparasci; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)

requirements.rationale: To freeze the hydrogen sample before melting it, the cell must reach below the hydrogen triple point, 13.8033 K.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Cryogenic Fixed Points (B Fellmuth, E Mendez-Lango, T Nakano, F Sparasci; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)

requirements.rationale: Isothermal conditions require the cell and its shields to be enclosed in a vacuum jacket.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Cryogenic Fixed Points (B Fellmuth, E Mendez-Lango, T Nakano, F Sparasci; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)
requirements.quote: To this end, the cell is surrounded by one or more temperature-controlled heat shields, the whole being enclosed in a vacuum jacket for thermal isolation.

requirements.rationale: The calorimetric method needs electrical heater pulses on the cell and four-wire leads to the thermometers under calibration.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Cryogenic Fixed Points (B Fellmuth, E Mendez-Lango, T Nakano, F Sparasci; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)

requirements.rationale: Preferred, not mandatory: modern realizations use closed-cycle cryocoolers allowing months of uninterrupted measurement; liquid-refrigerant cryostats were used traditionally.

requirements.quote: Nowadays preferably cryostats designed around closed-cycle cryocoolers are applied for the realization of cryogenic fixed points.

experiments.name: Realization of the ITS-90 from 3 K to 24.5561 K with a 3He/4He interpolating constant-volume gas thermometer calibrated at a helium vapour-pressure point (3.0-5.0 K), the e-H2 triple point and the neon triple point
experiments.plain_name: Measure very low temperatures from the pressure of helium gas sealed in a copper bulb
experiments.description: The ITS-90 between 3 K and the neon triple point is defined by an interpolating constant-volume gas thermometer: a bulb of typically one litre of OFHC copper filled with 3He or 4He, surrounded by an isothermal shield, with the pressure read through a ~1 mm capillary, calibrated at three temperatures and then used to calibrate rhodium-iron resistance thermometers.

requirements.rationale: The ICVGT defines the scale over 3 K to 24.5561 K and must be operated across that range.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Interpolating Constant-Volume Gas Thermometry (P P M Steur, B Fellmuth, O Tamura; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)
requirements.quote: In the range from 3 K to the triple point of neon (24.5561 K), the ITS-90 is defined in terms of a 3He or 4He constant-volume gas thermometer, CVGT, calibrated at three temperatures.

requirements.rationale: The lowest calibration point lies between 3.0 K and 5.0 K and the scale starts at 3 K, so the bulb must reach 3 K.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Interpolating Constant-Volume Gas Thermometry (P P M Steur, B Fellmuth, O Tamura; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)
requirements.quote: the values of p at the three fixed points (a point between 3.0 K and 5.0 K, 13.8033 K, 24.5561 K) are to be used to generate a quadratic interpolation function

requirements.rationale: Typical, not mandatory: the bulb is generally about one litre to reduce dead-space and adsorption effects, so the cold space must accommodate it.
requirements.document_title: Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Interpolating Constant-Volume Gas Thermometry (P P M Steur, B Fellmuth, O Tamura; BIPM CCT, last updated 1 January 2018)
requirements.quote: The volume of the bulb, VB, is generally large, typically one litre, to reduce dead-space effects (see Subsection 6) and to render adsorption effects negligible.

experiments.description: A sintered 3He melting-pressure cell with an in-situ capacitive pressure transducer is bolted to the experimental platform of an ultra-low-temperature refrigerator, filled through a CuNi capillary anchored at 1.5 K, the still (0.5 K), the base plate (0.06 K) and the mixing chamber, and read with a three-terminal capacitance bridge; the pressure is normalized at the minimum (315.24 mK) and, with a nuclear stage, at the Neel point (0.902 mK).
